text:
mike: heads up — getting a sustained p95/p99 latency spike on dedicated-pool-us-west starting ~12:05 UTC, SLA alerts firing :rotating_light:
emily: confirmed, p50 fine but p95 jumped 120ms -> ~850ms. throughput down ~30% on several tenants
infra-bot: [alert] dedicated-pool-us-west: GPU_util=95% mem=78% backpressure=ON
dan: looking at runtime logs — kernel fallback rate spiked at the same time. lots of "fallback_to_generic_kernel" messages and smaller batch sizes being emitted
sara: prefix cache metrics? could be KV cache thrash
mike: paste from metrics: `kv_prefix_hit_rate: 88% -> 15%`, `kv_evictions_per_min: 420 -> 2800`
alex: that eviction surge would force recompute of KV cache on many requests, explains latency tail and lower batching efficiency
dan: also seeing many allocations pinned to a single host (hotshard). placement shows a misbalanced placement decision - several minutes where autoscaler didn't add nodes
emily: timeline looks like: a quota change merged at 11:59 UTC that adjusted reserved_capacity flags for some tenants -> autoscaler skipped scale-up checks for that pool
mike: so two things: quota misconfig blocked scale-up, placement pinned work to fewer hosts -> noisy neighbor + KV thrash + kernel fallback + smaller batch packing = domino of perf regressions
sara: quick profiling snapshot I grabbed (trimmed):
```
kernel_select() counts: optimized_kernel=120 -> 18, generic_kernel=5 -> 217
batch_pack_efficiency: 0.78 -> 0.41
kv_load_latency_p50: 2ms -> 18ms
KV cache eviction trace: eviction spikes correlated with tenant x-heavy prefixes
```
dan: I traced a recent runtime change (deploy at 11:52) that adjusted kernel selection heuristics — combined with the hot placement it's causing higher fallback under partial cache misses
emily: immediate mitigation idea: revert kernel heuristic change to reduce fallback, force manual scale-up of dedicated-pool-us-west, and pin eviction-prone tenants off the hot host
mike: started manual scale-up now (requesting 4 nodes). also applied an emergency override to reserved_capacity for the pool so autoscaler can scale until config fixed
infra-bot: [action] scale_up requested -> 4 nodes pending allocation
alex: I kicked a migration to redistribute top 3 noisy tenants, started sequentially to avoid further thrash
sara: rolling back kernel heuristic change now (deploy rollback triggered)
dan: rollback complete, kernel fallback rate dropping in the tail metrics
emily: p95 improved to ~180ms within 3 minutes after rollback + scale-up, p99 trending down as migrations finish
mike: marking this as Sev-2; creating follow-up ticket to audit reserved_capacity flag logic and add canary to kernel-selection rollback safety
alex: suggest postmortem: root causes = 1) config change allowed reserved_capacity to block autoscaler 2) kernel-selection heuristic regression amplified the noisy-host effect 3) placement logic concentrated tenants -> KV cache thrash
sara: adding diagnostics we should keep: prefix-eviction alerts, kernel-fallback alert, placement-imbalance alert, and a small-runbook for manual migration steps
dan: notes for retro — avoid merging kernel heuristics and autoscaler/config changes in the same deploy window; add unit/regression tests for batch_pack_efficiency and fallback rate thresholds
mike: thanks all for quick responses. I'll follow up with the incident doc and assign owners for each follow-up item. :thumbsup:
